title: Abort in-flight navigation API traversals to pruned entries
body: Abort in-flight navigation API traversals to pruned entries When a same-document traversal is in flight and an intervening same-document navigation (e.g., `history.pushState()`) prunes the target entry from `navigation.entries()`, the spec previously continued applying the history step and hit an assertion failure during same-document navigation API entry updates. This change aligns with the Chromium and Ladybird implementations by: - Early-returning `false` from "fire a traverse `navigate` event" when `destinationNHE` is null during a same-document traversal (unless `navigation` has entries and events disabled), and rejecting any upcoming traverse API method tracker for that key with an `"AbortError"` `DOMException` without firing `navigate` or `navigateerror`. - Tracking when a descendant navigable's traverse `navigate` event aborts via an `aborted` flag on `changing navigable continuation state`, resetting its `ongoing navigation`, and skipping document activation and history/navigation API updates for that navigable. - Returning `"canceled-by-navigate"` from "apply the history step" if no changing navigable applied the step. Closes #12574. - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chromium * Gecko (https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12846#issuecomment-5492995677) * - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62214 * Note that `navigation-api/navigation-methods/forward-to-pruned-entry.html` also tests this - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: already works * Ladybird: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12846#issuecomment-6063827250 * Gecko: … * WebKit: … - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
